title: lean-tic-tac-toe, explained
h1: Tic-tac-toe in Lean 4, where an out-of-bounds move can't even be written down
lead: This is a small, playable tic-tac-toe program, not a theorem library. Its point is that the board's size lives in its type, so every cell lookup comes with a proof that the index is in range, and the game cannot crash on a bad index. Its one theorem, that a successful move changes exactly one empty square, is stated but unfinished: PARTIAL (sorry).
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of John Ericson's tic-tac-toe in Lean 4: size-indexed vectors and grids, move and win detection, a terminal game loop, and one unfinished (sorry'd) lemma.
startNote: Start with Vector, the size-carrying array everything else is built on. Then read Board.move and gameDone for the rules, and main for the game itself. The only theorem, movesAreValid, is unfinished: its proof ends in sorry.
sizeNote: About 470 lines of Lean in 7 files (about 290 of them outside the test file). It targets Lean 4.10 with Batteries.
agentCtx: A small Lean 4 tic-tac-toe game (any n×n board) built on size-indexed vectors, with a terminal frontend and one sorry'd lemma about moves.

gloss.Fin: Fin n is the type of natural numbers below n. Each value carries a proof that it is less than n.
gloss.Option: Option α is either some a (a value) or none (no value). Here it means "may fail".
gloss.Option.some: The "there is a value" case of Option.
gloss.Option.orElse: Keep the first option if it is some, otherwise run the fallback.
gloss.Nat.succ: Nat.succ k is k + 1. Writing a size this way forces it to be at least 1.
gloss.Fin.elim0: There is no element of Fin 0, so this case cannot happen.
